Our graphics display controller encountered screen tearing and frame buffer corruption during high-speed DMA streaming over the SPI interface. We connected a logic analyzer to the bus and observed that the DMA controller asserted a FIFO underrun flag in the stream status register. The firmware configured the DMA stream in direct mode without FIFO buffering, causing bus contention whenever the CPU accessed internal SRAM.

To eliminate the FIFO underruns, we updated the stream FIFO control register by setting the threshold to three-quarter FIFO instead. We also configured memory burst transfers by writing beat 4 into the MBURST field, so the DMA controller fetches 16 bytes per bus transaction.

Next, we modified the stream configuration register by raising the priority level from priority 1 to priority 3 instead. Write 0x01 into the transfer complete interrupt enable bit to signal the graphics engine upon frame transmission. After applying these register updates, the DMA stream maintained steady throughput without tearing artifacts during continuous frame buffer refreshes.

Our FreeRTOS flight controller suffered from task deadline overruns when sampling pressure sensors on the shared I2C bus. We traced the thread execution using Tracealyzer and discovered severe priority inversion between the sensor polling task and the data logging task. The logging thread grabbed a standard binary semaphore and began reading calibration registers by issuing repeated I2C transactions. While holding the lock, a medium-priority radio task preempted the logger, preventing it from releasing the semaphore and blocking the high-priority flight stabilization loop.

To resolve the priority inversion, we replaced the binary semaphore by creating a FreeRTOS mutex with priority inheritance enabled. When the high-priority loop blocks on the lock, the kernel elevates the logger priority to priority 5 instead. Write 30 into the mutex block time parameter to bound acquisition wait time.

We also configured the I2C timeout register by setting the SCL low timeout value to 35 milliseconds to abort frozen bus transactions. This scheduler redesign eliminated unbounded priority inversion across all sensor cycles during flight operation.

This non-blocking driver design preserved continuous watchdog feeding without timeout resets during flash erase operation.

Our smart energy meter dropped measurement pulses during high-frequency pulse train input under FreeRTOS. We monitored task execution using an event recorder and identified lost pulse events between the GPIO interrupt service routine and the pulse accumulation task. The interrupt handler was notifying the worker thread by calling task notify from ISR with the set-value-with-overwrite action. When two pulse interrupts occurred within 50 microseconds, the second event overwrote the notification register before the task unblocked.

We eliminated dropped pulse counts by updating the interrupt notification, switching the action parameter to increment so the notification behaves as an internal counting semaphore. We also configured the context switch by calling port yield from ISR instead whenever a higher-priority task wakes up.

Write 0xFF into the task notification clear mask by configuring the worker thread to decrement rather than clear the counter to 0. This scheduler fix restored accurate pulse tracking without missed energy counts during heavy electrical load calibration.
